tier_meaning.A: strong evidence for the scoped claim; multiple important controls or strong failure evidence
tier_meaning.A-: strong but with one material limitation such as preprint status, transfer scope, or incomplete replication
tier_meaning.B+: useful quantitative primary evidence with a material causal/reproducibility/generalization gap
tier_meaning.B: credible diagnostic or candidate evidence but intervention/ablation/replication remains incomplete
tier_meaning.B-: promising but important evidence is indirect, self-evaluated, or weakly isolated
tier_meaning.C+: primarily bottleneck/hypothesis evidence; not yet evidence for a working intervention
tier_meaning.C: supporting only; insufficient quantitative or causal extraction

assessments.note: Controlled artifact-visibility audit plus independent/internal failure evidence strongly supports full-trace/code audit need; online intervention itself remains untested.
AIRS-Bench gives strong scaffold comparison and public artifacts; AI-Scientist case study is weaker and compute/model separation is incomplete.
Large guidance-removal gap is strong bottleneck evidence, but no specific autonomous method-selection planner is causally validated.
Multiple failure analyses converge on protocol/evidence mismatch, but the proposed verifier intervention lacks a randomized or matched ablation.
PseudoBench provides strong adversarial failure signal; premise-gate implementation and false-rejection tradeoff are not demonstrated.
Agentic task/data generation has large quantitative separation and outer-loop improvement; transfer from data generation to full autonomous science is unverified.
Strong evidence that literature discovery is a bottleneck, but no demonstrated high-performing mechanism is attached to the candidate.
Scaled tournament/debate/evolve has quantitative self-evaluated Elo and domain validations, but lacks independent matched-budget causal isolation.
EvoAgentBench has matched vanilla controls, repeated runs, large positive oracle headroom and severe negative transfer; strong evidence for routing/admission constraints.
MAC is a broad controlled benchmark with explicit run variance and policy-violation failures; it remains a bounded proxy for recursive self-improvement.
MetaSkill-Evolve headline gains are primary, but marginal slow-loop ablation numbers are still secondary-source pending primary verification.
KSI has promising cross-model/project-page numbers and a clear persistent-object design, but exact primary tables and component ablations remain pending.
Meta-Harness has direct raw-trace versus scores/summary ablation, held-out transfer across models/tasks, and public artifact support; strongest causal evidence in this worker.
AutoDesign shows repeated matched harness attachment gains and independent dev acceptance, but the one-component-update restriction itself lacks a direct multi-component ablation.
RSEA directly ablates held-out gating, documents harmful unguarded evolution and safe fallback behavior; transfer sizes are modest in some cells.

PostTrainBench uses bounded compute, repeated runs, public trajectories and explicit integrity failures. Official-instruct comparison is not compute-matched, so use it as a capability/integrity benchmark rather than a human-efficiency claim.
Large component ablations and token/step efficiency deltas strongly support subgoal-local context organization in tested embodied benchmarks; external replication not established.
Matched baselines, multiple memory ablations, trained-vs-untrained helper evidence and held-out action model support selective intervention rather than indiscriminate memory injection.
Strong controlled negative evidence that more steps can hurt and that context locking occurs; CRNR itself lacks a safely extracted quantitative effect in the clean artifact.
Controlled inherited-trajectory manipulations and environment contrast support trajectory contamination risk; exact rate tables are incompletely extracted.
Peer-reviewed ICML evidence with extensive macro/subgoal/curriculum controls strongly supports reducing effective decision horizon within studied task families.
Useful long-run failure evidence against simple context-window exhaustion, but the artifact does not extract a strong intervention ablation or exact correlation statistic.
Mechanism is plausible and reportedly positive, but task-level numeric tables were not extracted; supporting evidence only until primary quantitative verification.
Matched-compute heterogeneous scaling and public code support diversity over raw N; exact per-task tables/variance are not extracted in the worker artifact.

arXiv v3 directly supports 260 configurations across six benchmarks, +80.8% to -70.0% range and 87% held-out architecture identification. Version-pin v3: older v1 summaries show 180/four and different R2.

CORAL has public code, strong kernel/multi-agent deltas and ablations, but headline SOTA/improvement-rate counts vary across paper versions/summaries and shared-memory/autonomy changes are partially confounded.
Peer-reviewed NeurIPS study provides direct niche-count and operator ablations with large degradations; exact K=4 optimum is scope-bound to tested population/tasks.
EvoMAS reports explicit pool/memory ablations and multiple benchmark gains; preprint status and some LLM-judge dependence limit certainty.
ICML primary evidence with strong continual baselines and regret/accuracy metrics supports world-model/planning separation under shared-dynamics reward-changing tasks.
Peer-reviewed theory plus neural experiments provide unusually strong negative evidence that replay quantity can increase forgetting; scope is carefully limited.
ICML quantitative comparisons are strong; transfer of K-FAC/Fisher replay behavior from vision OCL to autoregressive agents is unverified.
Peer-reviewed LLM continual-pretraining study is highly relevant, but exact replay-rate tradeoff tables were not extracted in the clean state.
Primary peer-reviewed claim is plausible and low-complexity, but exact LM deltas and replay interaction are still missing from the clean artifact.
ACL primary source spans multiple benchmarks/models, but headline numeric gain in state remains secondary-source pending primary table verification.
Matched raw-trajectory versus abstract-insight comparisons show strong directional negative/positive transfer; preprint and two-environment scope limit generalization.
LiveBench has strong objective/dynamic benchmark construction and reproducible infrastructure, but this is assurance-design evidence rather than a direct causal intervention on agent quality.
Controlled injected failures make judge reliability measurable and expose <55% accuracy; category-level breakdown and cross-agent transfer remain pending.
Exact transitivity/conformal statistics are strong per-instance diagnostics, but evidence is currently SummEval-specific and not yet agent-trace validated.
RewardBench 2 is strongly downstream-validated for Best-of-N across 113 reward models (r=0.87); PPO relation is explicitly distribution/lineage-sensitive.
OOD verifier results and label-efficiency deltas are useful, but candidate combines multiple sources/subsets and remains reasoning-domain concentrated.
Direct process-vs-outcome supervision evidence, active labeling and released 800k labels are strong; strongest demonstrated scope is mathematical reasoning.
Large-scale bias measurement is convincing, but mitigation efficacy is not directly ablated in the clean candidate.
Large multi-model studies support separating calibration from ranking/selective risk; no single universal estimator or intervention is established.
ICLR matched intrinsic-correction failures plus oracle-feedback positive controls sharply isolate the role of external correctness information.
Equal-response comparison directly shows debate underperforming self-consistency in the replicated GSM8K setup; scope is homogeneous agents/model and one task family.
Two primary studies plus retrieval blocking/manual leakage analyses strongly establish search-time contamination inflation on public benchmarks; rates are infrastructure-specific.
Paired counterfactual skill-vs-reference design and 307 attributed regressions are valuable; very recent preprint and budget-control details need closer verification.
Peer-reviewed ACL full-vs-partial trace comparison strongly supports observability for attribution; it does not show direct task-success improvement.
Author-confirmed benchmark defects and expert issue matching support automated benchmark audit, but evidence spans two scientific-agent benchmarks only.
Classic primary racing evidence has strong matched budget/selection statistics; transfer to research-agent candidate pruning is a hypothesis, not directly tested.
SATzilla gives strong per-instance routing gains with feature overhead accounted; modern research-orchestration transfer still needs out-of-sample validation.
Strong original theoretical/parallel-systems evidence, but agent-research transfer is indirect and depends on coarse independent tasks.
Nature primary evidence supports closed-loop mechanistic hypothesis testing in chemistry; scalar-performance causal advantage versus simpler optimizers is not fully isolated.
Mechanism has clear reproducible failure-minimization lineage, but the highlighted 114,019-to-1 case is a dramatic single case rather than average-case effect evidence.
Peer-reviewed Cell Reports transfer study is substantive, but exact broad-task tables are incompletely extracted and no independent replication was found.
Nature Communications provides multiple matched continual-learning results and replay/rehearsal interactions; frozen-feature setup and missing external replication limit transfer.
Strong peer-reviewed ablations and exact continual metrics support internal representation replay; feature extractor is frozen and external replication was not located.
PNAS evidence supports complementarity of gating and synaptic stabilization across long task sequences, but exact headline accuracies are not extracted and task-ID availability is a major constraint.
ICML primary results, broad architecture coverage and public code are strong; it is biological-plausibility evidence rather than continual-agent evidence and lacks independent replication.

RSIBench-Data has strong public runner/state artifacts and descriptive non-monotonic search statistics; direct causal comparison of best-ledger selection versus last-attempt deployment is not isolated.
AFTER reports a large multi-model-trace transfer advantage with benchmark artifacts; repository does not expose all experiment outputs and preprint replication is absent.
Public EvoAgentBench source-of-truth exposes large context-dependent gains/collapses and diagnostic anchor headroom; site reports means without standard errors in the cited artifact.
PAST-Bench provides runnable persistence on/off controls and mechanism ablations, but aggregate gain is noisy and five mechanisms are not established as additive.
Goedel-Prover-V2 has public code and strong verifier-guided repair/sample-efficiency results; token cost and exact component-ablation point values are incompletely extracted.
Fixed-sample structural-diversity comparison is unusually clean and includes strong counterevidence where the same intervention hurts an SFT prover, sharply bounding scope.
Peer-reviewed process-verifier RL has matched outcome/tactic/credit-placement ablations, compute reporting and mixed generalization evidence; strong scoped causal support.
Hierarchical decomposition has large module-swap and RL ablations plus public code/cheap-filter evidence; headline whole-proof comparison is not compute-matched.

P3 headline gains and targeted planning ablation are directly confirmed by the current primary arXiv source, but each task/model/method cell runs once and independent replication/open artifact evidence is not established.

cross_cutting_evidence_findings: The strongest repeated causal pattern is proposal/search separated from an independent acceptance or verification signal: RSEA, AutoDesign, theorem-verifier work, and failure studies all support this under different scopes.

Raw diagnostic traces repeatedly outperform compressed or output-only evidence for credit assignment/failure attribution, but this is not evidence that unrestricted trace retention is always optimal for cost or privacy.

Negative transfer is common enough to be a first-class evidence dimension: self-improvement skills, replay, memory injection, multi-agent topology, structural diversification, and extra-step scaling all have demonstrated harmful cells.
More compute/agents/steps is not monotone. Evidence favors conditional allocation based on task structure, verifier signal, held-out validation, or branch quality rather than unconditional scaling.

Version pinning matters for living preprints/benchmarks. Multi-agent scaling and PostTrainBench already show material revision/live-leaderboard drift; downstream use should preserve source version/date with every quantitative claim.
uncertainties: Most 2026 candidates are primary preprints with limited independent replication; tier A- should not be read as replicated consensus.
Public-code presence does not itself establish exact reproducibility; several candidates have artifacts but no clean independent rerun in this comparator.
Worker-reported numbers were not re-derived exhaustively from every primary table in this run; six high-impact/version-sensitive candidates received independent source spot checks.
